about: Verdict adjustments after the scan (post_rules.py) and comparison with the previous release (version_diff.py). rules are checked top to bottom and only the first match applies. applies_to is the scan verdict the rule looks at (any = all); verdict is the verdict when it matches.

rules.title: Release that OSV records as malicious (including releases removed from PyPI)
This release adds risky code the previous release did not have
A file that will be installed was recently added to an old release
Could not reach OSV (vulnerability and malware records) during the scan
Recent project with a name close to a popular package

known_malicious.about: OSV records that call this release malicious: an id prefix (OpenSSF malicious-packages) or the description text. The text counts only when the package itself is the subject (phrases like 'malicious URLs' that describe what a vulnerability enables are excluded).
known_malicious.text_regex: malicious code (in|was|were)|contain(s|ed)? malicious|embedded malicious|(is|are|was|were) considered malicious|(project|package|account)\b.{0,40}\bwas taken over|backdoored

typosquat.about: Name close to a popular package name (distance limits in scoring.json subscores.typosquat). Projects older than this are not suspected on the name alone.

new_package.about: Review if the project was first registered fewer than this many days ago.

osv_probe.about: Release queried to check that OSV actually answers. It must be one that always returns records when OSV works.
osv_probe.name: jinja2

version_diff.about: Whether this release adds risky code the previous release did not have. Uses only signals that ordinary updates rarely add.

signal_titles.import_time: New dangerous call that runs when the module is imported
signal_titles.new_pth: New .pth file with an import line
signal_titles.encoded_payload: New long encoded string together with decode, exec or write code

import_time.about: Dangerous calls that run when the module is imported (outside functions). builtins.* calls are skipped when the first argument is a constant string.

binary_py.detail: binary with a Python file name

encoded_payload.detail: long encoded string + exec, decode or write

transitive.about: Dependencies pulled in by the packages the command installs directly (transitive dependencies). Followed using PyPI metadata only to pick the version pip would choose (the locked version for lock installs); all of them are sent to OSV in one query to find malicious releases, and only releases uploaded within recent_days get a full scan, because hijacked releases are almost always fresh uploads.

late_file.about: A file pip will install was added long after the release came out, and recently.
